summary: @servicetitan/startup preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute an undeclared 727 KB obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex-suffixed identifiers such as `_0x19328d`, per-function object-literal indirection of every string constant and function call) and, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts the `bun` binary to a temp directory, and invokes it against `math_init.js` (`execFileSync(bun, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit'})`). math_init.js is a 727,680-byte heavily obfuscated bundle shipped at the tarball root; its header is `// @bun @bun-cjs` and its body is a large numeric/string constant array permuted by a rotate-shift decoder (`function WV8StW(...) {... MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift());... }`), which is the obfuscator.io string-array pattern. math_init.js is not listed in package.json `files` (which enumerates `bin, dist, eslint, jest, patches, src, tsconfig`), so it ships outside the author's declared manifest, and the filename does not match the package's advertised Lerna/TypeScript/React CLI purpose. Bun is fetched specifically so the payload executes under an alternate runtime rather than Node, evading Node-based inspection. The combination — obfuscated preinstall wrapper, alternate-runtime fetch, undeclared obfuscated sibling bundle executed on every install — is install-time arbitrary code execution on the installer's host with attacker-controlled content that cannot be inspected from the tarball.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
